## Components

- Installed: None. There is no primitive registry, no components.json and no shadcn/ui.
  Every surface is hand-written CSS against the `:root` token layer.
- Preferred primitives: None. Continue writing plain elements plus a scoped class or CSS
  module rather than introducing a component library.
- Tailwind v4 is installed and `@import "tailwindcss"` is app/globals.css line 1, but no
  Tailwind utility is used in the app. What Tailwind still contributes is its `base` layer
  (Preflight): the `box-sizing`/margin/padding/border reset, `list-style: none` on lists,
  `display: block` on replaced elements, `font-size`/`font-weight: inherit` on headings and
  `[hidden] { display: none !important }`. That reset is load-bearing for the whole visual
  system, so Tailwind cannot be removed by deleting utility usage alone.
- CSS modules (scoped, all consuming the same `:root` tokens):
  - components/announcements/announcements.module.css
  - components/coach/announcements/announcements.module.css
  - components/coach/dashboard-card.module.css
  - components/coach/financials/financial-records.module.css
  - components/coach/financials/financials.module.css
  - components/coach/junior-coach-dashboard.module.css
  - components/coach/onboarding/player-onboarding-register.module.css

## Tokens

All 54 tokens are declared in the single `:root` block at app/globals.css. Exactly one of them
is overridden in a narrower scope — `--portal-header-height` becomes `70px` inside a mobile
media query at app/globals.css:5763. For every other token, `var(--token)` and the token's
literal value are interchangeable anywhere in the document.

### Radius

The system is deliberately square: 19 declarations set `border-radius: 0` explicitly and are
left as literals, because a `--radius-none` token would say nothing the `0` does not.

- `--radius-xs`: `2px` (app/globals.css) — public form controls
- `--radius-sm`: `4px` (app/globals.css) — public buttons
- `--radius-pill`: `999px` (app/globals.css) — pills, dots and the ticket side notches, where
  it also appears in the two-corner forms `0 var(--radius-pill) var(--radius-pill) 0` and
  `var(--radius-pill) 0 0 var(--radius-pill)`
- `--radius-circle`: `50%` (app/globals.css) — avatars, initials, status dots, round controls
- Unadopted: one `border-radius: 3px` on `.submit-button` in app/public-home.css, which looks
  like drift against the `4px` public buttons. Reconciling it is a visual change, so it stays.

### Shadows

Only exact repeats are tokenised. The seven true drop shadows are all one-offs and are left as
literals — see Known drift below.

- `--shadow-keyline-lead`: `inset 3px 0 0 var(--red)` (app/globals.css) — the red leading

- `--shadow-keyline-bottom`: `inset 0 -3px 0 var(--red)` (app/globals.css) — the red bottom

- `--shadow-focus-ring`: `0 0 0 1px var(--navy)` (app/globals.css) — the navy focus ring on

### Layers

The z-index stack, named from the roles that already existed. Skip-link intentionally sits
above the dialog layer so it stays reachable.

- `--z-overlay`: `40` (app/globals.css) — public mobile-nav overlay
- `--z-header`: `50` (app/globals.css) — the portal and public sticky headers
- `--z-dialog`: `90` (app/globals.css) — coach report preview backdrop
- `--z-skip-link`: `100` (app/globals.css) — skip link
- `--z-admin-banner`: `1000` (app/globals.css) — platform-admin preview banner
- Not tokenised: the 15 local `z-index: 1`, `2` and `3` declarations. Those order siblings
  inside their own stacking context and have no relationship to the app-level stack; sharing a
  token would couple 15 unrelated sites.

### Breakpoints

Deliberately **not** tokens. A custom property cannot be used in a media query prelude —
`@media (max-width: var(--bp-md))` never matches, because media features are evaluated before
custom-property substitution. A `--bp-*` token would therefore be unusable at its only point
of use, and its existence would invite exactly that broken form. The project has no
`@custom-media` PostCSS plugin (only `@tailwindcss/postcss`), so the widths are recorded here
instead.

The 20 distinct widths in use, by frequency:

- Primary: `720px` (17), `980px` (13), `760px` (11), `900px` (10)
- Paired minimums: `721px` (7), `761px` (5), `780px` (1), `901px` (1)
- Small mobile: `360px` (5), `340px` (4), `380px` (3), `430px` (1), `320px` (1)
- Occasional: `1100px` (3), `820px` (2), `1000px` (1), `860px` (1), `700px` (1), `640px` (1),
  `600px` (1)

`720px`/`721px`, `760px`/`761px` and `900px`/`901px` are the intended pairs. The singletons
(`1000px`, `860px`, `820px`, `780px`, `700px`, `640px`, `600px`, `430px`, `380px`) are drift
rather than system steps; do not treat them as a scale.

Reconciling any of these would change rendered output, so they are documented, not changed.

- Seven drop shadows, no two alike, three of them near-duplicates that were almost certainly

  `0 32px 90px rgba(3, 15, 28, 0.34)` (`.coach-report-preview`),
  `0 16px 38px color-mix(in srgb, var(--navy) 8%, transparent)` (`.ledgerTicket`) and
  `10px 0 20px rgba(7, 27, 50, 0.04)` (sticky register name column).
- Transition durations `140ms`, `150ms` and `160ms` coexist for the same kind of background
  and colour change.
- `border-radius: 3px` on `.submit-button` against `4px` on the other public buttons.
- ~~Two dead rules reference custom properties that are defined nowhere.~~ **Resolved:** the
  `.player-attendance-register-table` block and its two undeclared custom properties were removed
  in the dead-selector pass, along with 23 unreachable class keys in
  components/coach/financials/financials.module.css left over from the financials-to-modules
  migration — 693 net lines. The token test no longer needs its allowlist for them.
- A third visually-hidden implementation still exists as a scoped rule rather than a utility:
  `.personal-attendance-calendar .player-attendance-month-nav span` in app/globals.css. It is
  the only one that already carries both `clip` and `clip-path`. Folding it into `.sr-only`
  needs component edits inside the frozen calendar surfaces.

### Accessibility utility

`.sr-only` is defined locally in app/globals.css, immediately after the `touch-action` rule,
and is the single visually-hidden utility. It replaces both Tailwind's `sr-only` and the former
`.coach-published-visually-hidden`. It is declared unlayered and `!important` so that it
outranks the ~14,000 unlayered lines below it; a Tailwind utility-layer class cannot, because
unlayered CSS beats every cascade layer regardless of specificity.

## Constraints

### Must

- Feel like a personal training journal rather than admin software
- Keep functional metrics below the welcome hero
- Reuse SMBA ivory, navy, red, Manrope, Newsreader, and official logo

### Avoid

- Dense KPI grids
- Admin sidebars
- Decorative animation
- Generic sports gradients

## Decisions

- **dashboard-entry**: Use a near-full-height personal welcome with a time-aware greeting and one editorial coach message; reveal dashboard functions only after the fold.
- **navigation**: Keep the portal centered on one primary page with no tab navigation. A single Monthly reports card leads from the dashboard to one continuous coach-report record, with a contextual back action returning to the dashboard.
- **motion**: Use short opacity and transform reveals only, with reduced-motion fallbacks and no scroll-jacking.
- **monthly-reports**: Use the selected Concept 01 Season Ledger for Monthly reports. Keep report content off the landing page and open one chronological archive organized as calendar-year chapters. Each chapter begins with a compact Season record masthead, an editorial year and its local coach-report count; rows beneath it use restrained red folio numbers that reset within each year, a consistently aligned month, publication date and disclosure control. The newest report year opens by default, older years remain collapsed, individual reports begin collapsed, and only one year and one report may be open at a time. Selecting a month reveals the navy coach-feedback reading panel and one outlined PDF action inline, with the label, copy and action sharing a deliberate alignment axis across desktop, tablet and mobile. Group by the report month rather than publication year, preserve selected chapter and report in URL state, and keep downloaded PDFs in the separate A4 academy letterhead format.
- **player-reflection**: Do not include an on-screen training journal. SMBA provides a physical notebook in the welcome kit so players can reflect away from screens during sessions.
- **coach-workspace**: Use a separate /coach route and coach-specific shell. Treat its calm near-full-height hero as a morning briefing rather than a dashboard: a personalized greeting, one short encouraging operational line, one ivory daily briefing card, and a scroll cue into attendance. The encouragement stays specific to the coach's role and supports readiness without becoming sentimental or performance-driven. The hero remains editorial rather than analytical. Any future hero metric must answer an immediate operational question for today; historical trends, reporting, notifications, and general KPIs belong below the fold.
- **coach-dashboard-hero-scoreboard-ribbon**: Use the selected Scoreboard Ribbon composition for the head-coach welcome. Desktop keeps the oversized greeting above one full-width ivory daily ribbon with a prominent date, a centered today’s-session count, a visible First session or Next session label beneath the time, and clearly spaced first/next-on-court context. Tablet and 341–980px mobile layouts use a compact two-by-two ribbon: date and on-court context share the top row while session count and time share the bottom row. At 340px and below, return to a stacked reading order to protect legibility. Mobile preserves the oversized greeting across the navy area, with one quiet orthographic badminton-court diagram behind it. Keep the hero operational and editorial; do not add historical metrics, generic KPI cards, decorative navigation or perspective court graphics.
- **player-dashboard-hero-scoreboard-ribbon**: Keep the Player Journal hero personal rather than operational. Preserve the oversized time-aware greeting over the quiet orthographic court, but let the ivory ribbon contain only the current message from Coach Sathiya. Do not repeat next-session date, time, duration or other training logistics in the hero; the complete Next Session briefing belongs in the first dashboard card below. Desktop and tablet use a balanced attribution-and-quotation ribbon, while mobile stacks the attribution above the quotation for legibility.
- **shared-scoreboard-hero-rhythm**: Keep the player and head-coach scoreboard heroes visually paired through the same navy field, quiet orthographic court, oversized greeting rhythm, desktop ribbon minimum height and fully visible 44px scroll cue at the 390 by 844 mobile viewport. Their ribbon content may differ by role: the coach retains operational training information, while the player receives only the coach's editorial message.
- **coach-dashboard-card-system**: Use the selected Concept 01 Court Operations Board for the seven head-coach dashboard workflows. Place all cards in one shared responsive ticket grid with fine borders, clipped circular notches, dashed mastheads, restrained red state stamps, Newsreader status statements and explicit navy-outlined action boxes. Attendance remains the first full-width workflow beneath the hero, visibly separates Player and Staff destinations, and owns the hero's Today's attendance cue and #attendance target. Player Onboarding follows immediately as the second full-width ticket inside the same ivory card field—without a separate divider—so it reads as another dashboard workflow rather than a detached section. It summarizes the exclusive New requests, Assessment, Session and Fee plan stages before one boxed Open onboarding action. Desktop places Sessions beside Monthly Reports, followed by equal Financials, Announcements and Members cards. Tablet keeps Attendance, Onboarding and Sessions full width, then pairs Monthly Reports with Financials and Announcements with Members so no orphaned column space remains. Mobile stacks the same accessible order: Attendance, Player Onboarding, Sessions, Monthly Reports, Financials, Announcements and Members. Members is a directory-only card; approval and progress states belong to Player Onboarding. Preserve every dynamic, empty, complete, inactive, attention, preparation and pending state, every destination, report-resume behavior and the #attendance scroll target. This decision supersedes only the older frozen Coach Dashboard card presentation; attendance registers, calendar workspaces and their mobile contracts remain unchanged.
- **coach-player-onboarding-next-step-register**: Use the selected Next-Step Register at /coach/onboarding as the single owner of player approval, court assessment, recurring-session assignment and Fee Plan creation. Derive the four exclusive New requests, Assessment, Session and Fee Plan counts and the ordered player list from one classifier, ordered by next required step and then oldest waiting player. Use one continuous ruled register with restrained red Newsreader folios, player identity, a factual stage stamp, one clear next-action sentence and one 44px boxed expander. Exactly one row opens inline. The expansion uses an accessible Request–Assessment–Session–Fee Plan progress rail and exposes only the current operation: approve or reject, Level/Batch/Training plan, matching schedule/days/effective date, or agreed monthly fee/track-from month. Reuse the canonical guarded service actions; never recreate approval, assignment or financial invariants in the client. Preserve Academy-ID copy fallback, URL-backed selection, field errors, optimistic revisions, unsaved-work protection, finance-inactive and no-schedule recovery links, focus restoration, a durable all-complete shell and zero horizontal overflow. Desktop uses aligned register columns and a vertical progress rail, tablet keeps the expansion attached below its row, and mobile uses a 2x2 count strip, compact numbered slips, a horizontal four-step rail and stacked 48px controls. Label playerEnrollments.academyPlan as Training plan so it cannot be confused with the monetary Fee Plan.
- **portal-architecture**: Run the public homepage, Player Journal and Coach Workspace as one Next.js application and one session boundary. The public academy remains at /, players enter at /player, coaches enter at /coach, and protected areas retain dedicated layouts over the same academy database.
- **unified-application**: Preserve the established public and portal visual systems while consolidating them under one server, one domain and one login-aware header. Keep the former site project only as a temporary rollback copy; do not duplicate business data or authentication across applications.
- **prototype-login**: Use one Academy ID login for both roles. Public registration is player-only, remains inaccessible until coach approval, and receives an immutable human-friendly Academy ID after approval. Coach access requires a future controlled provisioning flow rather than self-selected registration. The cookie stores only a random database-backed session token. Academy ID authentication is explicitly a guarded local prototype that can be replaced by OTP without changing account UUIDs, Academy ID allocations or academy history.
- **new-student-state**: Treat prototype sign-in as a genuine first-day student experience: identity is personalized, while program, level, attendance, sessions and monthly reports remain pending until assessment or training creates them. Use calm empty states and one assessment action instead of invented performance data.
- **coach-attendance**: Make attendance the first workflow beneath the coach welcome. The annual school-register view is selected by Weekday or Weekend Batch and Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced or Adult Level. A player appears as one group with a separate sub-row for every assigned session, so two occurrences on one day remain independently markable and count as two eligible sessions. Allow marking only where an immutable scheduled occurrence exists, the assignment covers it, the occurrence is on or after joining, and it is not cancelled or in the future. Keep explicit draft saving, unsaved-change protection, India date rules and previous/current/next year navigation.
- **coach-calendar**: Use the SMBA Session Calendar as the operational source of truth. Session-series UUIDs are immutable identities; Level_Batch_Time display names are generated consistently for presentation. Level plus Weekday or Weekend Batch determines assignment eligibility, while assignments determine participation. Players may hold multiple matching, non-overlapping active assignments. Late assignment exposes only real occurrences from its effective date, attendance always references immutable occurrences, and cancellation or replacement preserves history. Google Calendar remains a future optional synchronization layer.
- **coach-training-operations**: Separate operations from configuration. Calendar opens on today and uses its month grid only as a navigator into the Day View workspace, where attendance and occurrence actions live. Schedules is the single place for recurring session configuration, player assignments and rosters. On a normal Schedules entry, all programme groups begin collapsed; a guided player-assignment link may still open the relevant programme and session directly. Do not reintroduce Agenda or Week views.
- **academy-plans-and-assignment-days**: Keep Academy Plan as an informational enrollment and pricing choice: Weekday 3-day, 4-day or 5-day, and Weekend plan. It never creates attendance or participates in attendance calculations. During session assignment, Weekday plans require an exact union of 3, 4 or 5 distinct weekdays across all active assignments; Weekend retains its current one-or-two-day flexibility. The first Weekday assignment establishes the complete training week, later assignments may reuse those days, and the saved effective-dated assignment weekdays independently determine which immutable session occurrences are attendance-eligible. Completing a player's first evaluation leads directly into this assignment workflow.
- **coach-reports**: Split Coach Reports into two explicit tasks without changing the immutable report model. Write Reports is the operational workspace for drafts, resume, editing, preview and publication; Published Reports is a month-first, read-only archive of immutable publication revisions with exact-revision detail and private PDF downloads. The Dashboard card keeps the latest completed reporting-month progress and exposes both destinations with equal weight. The writer retains the Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced and Adult checklist, last selected player and month, read-only attendance, unsaved-work protection and one-to-two-paragraph editor. The archive defaults to the latest completed India reporting month, includes archived players' history, never exposes drafts, and preserves revision identity through publication UUIDs.
- **coach-published-reports-court-register**: Use the selected Court Register format for the head-coach Published Reports archive. Keep a compact title and reporting-month navigator, followed by one count-and-search utility rail and one continuous ordered register with restrained red folios, player identity, revision history, publication date and separate Open report and PDF actions. Desktop uses aligned register columns with side-by-side actions; tablet combines revision and updated date while stacking actions; mobile turns each entry into three legible bands for identity, revision/date and two equal actions. Keep the archive read-only and preserve exact immutable revisions, archived-player labels, name or Academy ID search, return-state URLs, distinct empty states and 10-at-a-time progressive reveal with visible status and keyboard focus restoration.
- **coach-members**: Use the selected Concept 01 Court Roster Register for the coach-only Member Directory as a directory-only academy record. Begin directly with one search-and-filter utility rail and one continuous ruled member register; registration approval and incomplete onboarding states live exclusively in Player Onboarding. Reuse the restrained red two-digit folio system from Published Reports so visible members retain a stable scan order as the directory reveals twelve more at a time. Desktop aligns Member, combined Training, Sessions, Joined, Status and Details as compact columns; tablet turns each member into two aligned bands; mobile uses one compact slip with the folio rail, identity and status, training facts, sessions and joined date, then a full-width Details disclosure. Keep one expanded record at a time and preserve URL-backed filters, privacy-first contact reveal, editing and revision guards, assignment locks, non-destructive archival, empty states and keyboard focus restoration. Member edits save in place and never redirect into first-time assignment. Current session assignments remain the source of training status.
- **academy-data-lifecycle**: Treat Account, Authentication and Player Enrollment as separate domains. Immutable account UUIDs own historical relationships; Academy IDs are never reused or edited. Player enrollment moves from Unassigned to Active or Paused, while archive is an administrative state. Attendance clearing is recorded as a state and published report revisions remain immutable rather than being deleted or overwritten.
- **attendance-integrity**: Calculate monthly attendance through one pure Asia/Kolkata date-only domain service with an injected reference date. Eligibility requires an immutable scheduled occurrence covered by the player's assignment, on or after their joining date and on or before the reference date. Unmarked sessions remain pending and do not reduce the recorded rate. Live workspaces share saved attendance, while every immutable report publication stores an append-only versioned attendance snapshot so later corrections never rewrite an older report or PDF.
- **attendance-adjustments**: Keep routine marking and exceptional reconciliation as separate focused destinations reached from the Coach Dashboard Attendance card. Record attendance opens the occurrence-based annual register at /coach/attendance; Reschedule attendance opens the existing make-up editor at /coach/attendance/adjustments. Both destinations share the same Back to dashboard placement, Attendance register eyebrow, title alignment, title-to-workspace gap and bordered workspace start. Inside the rescheduling workspace, do not repeat a second visible Make-up attendance title or a redundant Draft badge. Use a quiet New adjustment eyebrow that changes to Review adjustment during review, while a screen-reader-only heading preserves structure. Keep the first Player control close to that eyebrow and render action feedback only when a message exists. Review confirmation uses coach-facing action language—Ready to reschedule attendance—rather than exposing attendance-accounting mechanics; publication confirms Attendance rescheduled. After the coach chooses a player, select the source absence from a compact month calendar rather than a long list: the coach may move directly between months containing absences, missed dates use a restrained red ring, a selected date can be tapped again to clear it and its dependent draft values, and a date with multiple saved absences reveals the exact session occurrences. When a player has no unreconciled absence, replace the calendar with one compact 52px information strip rather than preserving calendar-sized empty space. A published make-up links one saved absence to one completed academy training date without changing schedules, assignments, rosters or eligibility. Keep that evidence inside the original session row: the source cell becomes a quiet ochre state without a letter marker, while the completion date shows an inline green +N in the same row. Do not add a separate make-up row. 
- **attendance-adjustments-2**: Previous reschedules remain collapsed until requested, published or deep-linked. Their collapsed rows show white status boxes with semantic outlines only; hovering anywhere on a collapsed row shades the surrounding bar beige while the box interior remains white. The destructive Void adjustment action appears inside expanded details as one full-width red outline with a pale hover tint. Drafts remain local and protected, publication is explicit, reversals are soft-voided, and legacy dashboard adjustment URLs redirect to the focused rescheduling page.
- **training-language**: Do not use invented foundation, development or competitive pathways. Describe training with the academy's factual Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced and Adult programs, together with batch and active status. Age groups remain deferred until the academy defines them.
- **mobile-operational-density**: Preserve the spacious public, Player Journal and Coach Workspace welcome experiences, but make mobile operational pages task-first and content-driven. Keep the first useful action within the initial viewport, place Next session before attendance and reports for players, place attendance directly beneath the coach briefing, and use progressive disclosure for optional filters, report queues and long schedule groups. Compactness must come from removing repetition and idle space rather than shrinking touch targets or changing SMBA's editorial visual identity.
- **coach-calendar-workspace-density**: Treat Day View as a coach's running sheet rather than a marketing page. Its reading order is time, session identity, then operational status. On mobile, gain density through tighter internal rhythm and stable alignment while preserving typography, touch targets, logical-group whitespace, expanded-session continuity and the current desktop balance. Session metadata uses calm sentence case, and cancelled occurrences remain clearly legible rather than fading through whole-row opacity.
- **coach-calendar-date-selection**: Keep the selected calendar date quiet rather than filling the full cell navy: use the existing light ivory token as a subtle beige wash with a crisp two-pixel navy inset frame. Identify the actual India-local today independently with one small coral dot, and reserve the coral outline for visible keyboard focus. Ordinary session counts stay steel so red retains operational meaning. Preserve aria-pressed for selection and aria-current=date for today.
- **public-production-readiness**: Treat the approved public homepage as a locked editorial composition. Production polish may correct factual drift, semantics, focus, touch targets, essential helper-text legibility, responsive asset delivery and metadata without restructuring sections or changing SMBA's visual identity. Keep public motion subtle and CSS-native where it can preserve the same experience with less client payload.
- **mobile-authentication-freeze**: Treat the validated mobile Login and Registration experience as frozen. Preserve its shared field spacing, typography, controls, copy, whitespace and structure. Subsequent changes are limited to functional bugs, accessibility regressions or production defects; any visual redesign requires a separate milestone.
- **mobile-account-menu-freeze**: Clamp long signed-in names to two naturally wrapped lines in the authenticated mobile portal menu while retaining the complete name in the DOM. Preserve both portal and public account-menu width, positioning, spacing, controls, wording and interaction behavior. Subsequent mobile changes are limited to functional bugs, accessibility regressions or production defects; desktop enhancements require a separate milestone.
- **mobile-calendar-attendance-freeze**: Treat the validated mobile Coach Dashboard, Session Calendar, Month View, Day View, expanded session roster, Attendance Register, empty day state and Attendance dashboard card as frozen. Preserve their operational hierarchy, navigation, typography, touch targets, annual-register structure and desktop presentation. Subsequent changes are limited to functional defects, accessibility regressions, production issues or evidence gathered from observed coach usage; visual or workflow redesign requires a separate milestone.
- **coach-dashboard-attendance-entry**: Present the Coach Dashboard Attendance entry with the same two-box destination pattern as Sessions. Keep Attendance register as a small eyebrow above a single horizontal row containing the register icon and Attendance title; this attendance-specific title arrangement does not alter the Sessions card. Retain the schedule count, then provide matched links for Record attendance and Reschedule attendance. Each link opens a dedicated focused page; the dashboard card itself does not expand. Preserve the established card typography, borders, action hierarchy and all register, adjustment, deep-link and unsaved-work behavior inside their respective destinations.
- **coach-attendance-mobile-level-selector**: Keep all four attendance levels visible together on mobile in a compact two-by-two grid. Do not require horizontal scrolling to discover Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced or Adult. Preserve the existing selected state, typography and touch-target height; the Weekday and Weekend batch selector remains a separate two-option row.
- **coach-attendance-year-selector**: Present four year values directly without a redundant Year label: the previous year, current year and next two years. Derive them from the current India calendar year so the range advances automatically. Keep the values as equal-width mobile controls with the existing selected-state styling and touch-target height.
- **coach-attendance-selected-category-heading**: Keep the selected Level and Batch value on one deliberate line throughout the 320–430px mobile range. Scale only this editorial heading responsively so Intermediate with either Weekday or Weekend remains intact; preserve selector typography, register structure and desktop heading scale.
- **mobile-member-directory-freeze**: Treat the validated mobile Member Directory landing, search, filters, filtered results, member cards, expand and collapse interaction, member details, contact reveal, edit form and 320–430px responsive layouts as frozen. Preserve the privacy-first contact treatment, Profile and Training hierarchy, initials, status presentation, navigation, density and established coach-workspace interaction model. Expansion-control weight, expanded-panel separation and active-filter emphasis remain deferred unless accessibility review or observed coach usage establishes a concrete need. Subsequent changes are limited to functional defects, accessibility regressions, production issues or evidence gathered from coach usability testing; aesthetic or structural revisions require a separate milestone.
- **member-directory-production-integrity**: Preserve the frozen Member Directory composition while hardening its production behaviour. Member edits use an explicit record revision and never write assignment-managed status; validation and assignment invariants are enforced transactionally; Academy ID presentation comes from the immutable allocation rather than an active login method; contact reveal restores focus and reconceals on collapse; and non-destructive archival is allowed only after active assignments end, revoking login access while preserving all academy history.
- **financials-v1**: Treat Financials as a quiet operational ledger rather than an accounting dashboard. Charges, payments and append-only adjustments are immutable facts; balances and statuses are always derived. The coach receives a focused current-month workspace and quick payment flow after Monthly Reports, while the player receives a subordinate read-only Fee Record after reports. Financial state never controls training, attendance, scheduling, reports or account access. Preserve SMBA's existing cards, typography and compact mobile operational rhythm; do not introduce charts, collection pressure, automated reminders or finance metrics in either welcome hero.
- **financials-v2**: Extend the quiet Financials ledger with human-readable receipts, immutable multi-charge allocations, refunds and fee concessions without turning it into an accounting dashboard. Quick Record Payment is the coach's primary repeated workflow; the player sees a restrained read-only receipt history with allocation, refund and neutral Fee concession facts. Receipt and refund corrections use explicit reversal workflows, published allocations never mutate, balances remain derived from ledger facts, and CSV collection history is generated on demand. Reuse the established bordered cards, typography, status language, notices and mobile density; do not introduce charts, aging reports, reminders, gateways, invoice PDFs or new dashboard metrics.
- **financials-v3**: Complete Financials as a coach-maintained current-truth record system without turning SMBA into accounting software. Add one Financial Records destination containing the calculator-backed Fee Register, Collections Day Book and readable Activity History; generate private receipt and player-statement PDFs and formula-safe CSV exports on demand without persistence or ledger writes. End Fee Plans explicitly and auditably, and restart through a new non-overlapping effective-dated agreement rather than rewriting history. Preserve the established bordered operational language and the Player Portal experience. Do not add gateways, checkout, expenses, payroll, GST, period-close snapshots, reminders, charts or financial hero metrics.
- **player-attendance-record**: Keep the player-facing annual attendance register read-only and visually aligned with the coach register. Present and absent use calm solid green and solid red cells respectively; do not add ticks, crosses or decorative patterns to recorded states. Pending uses a short muted horizontal dash, while future scheduled cells remain quiet ivory without a symbol. Player-facing adjustment language is Rescheduled. The adjacent text legend provides the explicit status labels.
- **player-attendance-focused-month-calendar**: This decision supersedes only the year-wide horizontal presentation in player-attendance-record. Keep Annual attendance as the expanded ticket context and retain direct year controls, but show one selected month at a time in a Monday-first seven-column calendar. Previous and next month controls flank a centered, non-interactive month-and-year label; do not add a dropdown, miniature month-summary grids or a decorative rule through the toolbar. Preserve URL-backed open, month and year state, browser history and Jump to today. Use the selected Editorial Split for the workspace heading: keep Your record and Annual attendance together on the left, and align the year selector with Jump to today in one vertically centered control row on desktop and tablet. On mobile, stack the title, a full-width year selector, then Jump to today. A date may contain several independent assigned-session marks, so never collapse same-day occurrences into one status. Preserve solid green Present, solid red Absent, a muted Pending dash, quiet future sessions, ochre Rescheduled sources, green +N completions, explicit adjacent text legend and complete accessible date labels. Adjacent-month dates may mute only their date labels; recorded attendance colours remain full strength, so Present is the same solid green everywhere. The calendar must fit without document-level or local horizontal scrolling at supported widths. Keep these player-specific session and rescheduling semantics out of the head-coach operational registers.
- **player-next-session**: Present the Player Journal's Next Session card as the full-width anchor of the selected Match Tickets composition. Use one text-led ticket masthead with a restrained red date stamp, then read through start time, date, session identity and practical details before a pale perforated arrival-note stub on desktop and tablet; stack that note beneath the briefing on mobile. Preserve the existing time-aware occurrence resolution and every empty state. Do not add a decorative icon, countdown, action or motion.
- **player-dashboard-companion-cards**: Use the selected 04A.1 Compact Match Tickets composition for the Player Dashboard cards, with no redundant visible section introduction. Desktop places the full-width Next Session ticket above an equal Attendance, Monthly Reports and Fee Record trio; tablet keeps Attendance shallow and full-width above half-width Reports and Fee tickets; mobile stacks the same reading order. Use fine borders, clipped circular ticket notches, dashed mastheads, restrained red context stamps and explicit navy-outlined actions labelled Open attendance record, Open report records and Open fee record. The Attendance action remains the URL-backed disclosure button, while Reports and Fee use those boxes as their sole link targets rather than whole-card links. Preserve percentage, progress, loaded, pending, paused, unavailable and empty states. Optional Announcements follow the primary four as one full-width compatible ticket. Begin the card section one compact spacing group after the hero and keep a viewport-height landing area so the training-week cue aligns directly below the sticky portal header, avoids a stranded navy strip or cue row, and keeps the passive player ledger visible on desktop and tablet.
- **player-dashboard-announcements-card**: Use an adaptive full-width Match Ticket for Player Dashboard announcements. Preserve the total active-notice count in the red masthead stamp and retain direct links to each visible notice, but preview at most the pinned-first, newest-first top two. One notice uses a featured editorial layout with its shared archive action beside it on desktop and tablet. Two notices sit side by side with a quiet dashed divider on desktop and tablet, then stack on mobile. Close every populated state with one navy-outlined Open all announcements action; for the two-notice state it spans the card below both previews. Keep content-to-action spacing compact. A successful zero-notice result keeps the ticket visible as the selected Quiet all-clear state: use a Clear stamp, the Newsreader message The notice board is clear, and one muted explanatory sentence; do not add an eyebrow, icon or archive action that leads to an empty destination. Keep query failure as a separate isolated unavailable state, and do not alter the other dashboard tickets or player ledger.
- **player-profile-ledger**: Close the Player Journal dashboard with a quiet editorial ledger for Player, Level and Academy Plan. Use compact labelled rows on mobile and content-proportional columns on desktop, retaining the semantic description list and natural wrapping. Keep this passive reference information visually subordinate to the dashboard cards; do not add a title, icon, credential treatment, action or decorative motif. Academy Plan presentation does not repeat the separately labelled Level.
- **coach-financials-task-navigation**: Organize coach Financials around two explicit tasks rather than a combined landing workspace. Record Payment is the rapid receipt workflow and defaults to players with outstanding balances while allowing an All players fallback. Fee Records is the administrative destination for the Fee Register, Collections Day Book, Activity History and focused per-player fee records containing plans, registration reconciliation, concessions, ledger history and corrections. The Coach Dashboard card exposes both destinations and the current month preparation state. For active academies, /coach/financials remains only a compatibility redirect; inactive academies retain the setup flow. Preserve all ledger facts, calculations, audit rules and player-facing financial presentation.
- **coach-record-payment-balance-line**: Use the selected Option 01 Balance Line for the coach Record Payment page. Before selection, use one full-width finder ledger with the title, search and Outstanding or All players controls on a compact utility rail; do not reserve an empty payment or receipt pane. Its result list begins collapsed, expands as a two-column register on desktop and tablet, and returns to one column on mobile. Once a payable player is selected, replace the directory with one compact payer rail containing identity, status, outstanding balance and a guarded Change player action. Make outstanding minus amount received equal projected balance the primary visual relationship, followed by one ruled metadata strip and one compact allocation review within the same white ledger. On desktop and tablet, center each equation operand, its amount and supporting line beneath the existing centered operators; center only the bounded Selected player and Outstanding utility cells in the payer rail. Keep the player identity, editable metadata, allocation descriptions, totals and action bars on stable scan axes rather than centering the entire form. On desktop, keep all payment metadata in one readable row, use a minimum 10–11px operational text floor for labels and supporting facts, and let an unpaired allocation row span the full ledger rather than leaving a false empty cell. Stack the equation's labelled values on mobile without shrinking touch targets. Returning to Change player restores the URL-backed finder; successful recording returns to that finder and preserves existing focus, validation, allocation, idempotency and unsaved-work behaviour.
- **coach-registration-fee-entry-register**: Use the selected 01 Academy Entry Register for Registration fees inside coach Fee Records. Present the one-time academy entry count beside the explicit net registration fees minus received equals outstanding relationship, then a compact filter rail and a continuous numbered register. Each entry preserves player identity, Academy ID, fee reference or Not prepared state, due or no-charge context, exact non-zero credit and debit adjustments, charged, received, balance, status, archived marker and an explicit Open record action. Desktop uses one aligned ruled table; tablet reflows each entry into a compact multi-band register row; mobile uses a narrow folio slip with identity, status, entry facts, all three amounts and the full-width action. Folio numbers are visible-page scan aids rather than record identifiers. Maintain a readable operational type floor of approximately 10px for labels and supporting facts and 12px for row values; gain compactness by shortening idle padding and page gaps rather than shrinking controls or hiding ledger facts. Preserve the existing URL-backed filters, CSV export, pagination, focused-record context, empty states and ledger semantics. This decision governs Registration fees; the paired Monthly Fee Cycle Register governs Monthly fees, while Collections and Activity retain their own compositions.
- **coach-monthly-fee-cycle-register**: Use the Monthly Fee Cycle Register for Monthly fees inside coach Fee Records. Present the selected month and record count beside the explicit net monthly fees minus received equals outstanding relationship, followed by one compact monthly-preparation docket, URL-backed filters and a continuous numbered register. Each row preserves player identity, Academy ID, monthly fee reference or Not prepared state, due or no-charge context, exact non-zero credit and debit adjustments, billed, received, balance, status, archived marker and an explicit Open record action. Desktop uses one aligned ruled table; tablet reflows each entry into a compact multi-band register row; mobile keeps the narrow folio rail, identity and status, monthly-fee facts, three amounts and a full-width action without horizontal scrolling. Folios are visible-page scan aids rather than record identifiers. Maintain the same readable type floor and responsive grammar as Registration fees, while retaining monthly preparation, month selection, CSV export, pagination, focused-record context, empty states and all ledger semantics. Do not add a separate KPI grid or hide preparation states to gain density.
- **coach-focused-player-fee-register**: Extend the Academy Entry Register language into the focused coach player fee record without changing finance behaviour. Replace the oversized navy player hero with one compact white identity docket and an adjacent ivory outstanding-status cell, then retain the fee plan as a short ruled facts band. Present first-time Create fee plan and effective-dated Change fee plan as compact ruled dockets: keep Level, Batch and Academy Plan in one facts strip, keep fee and month fields together, and place one clear action beside or directly below them by breakpoint. Present receipts and charges as separate continuous numbered registers with restrained red folios, readable 10px supporting text and 12px-or-larger values; folios remain display-only scan aids. Desktop and tablet align each record across fine rules, while mobile keeps a narrow folio rail and stacks amounts into two columns without horizontal scrolling. Keep receipts, refunds, concessions, fee-plan validation and unsaved-work guards, payment history, corrections, downloads, archived safeguards and derived balances intact. Gain density through reduced idle padding and gaps, never by hiding ledger facts or shrinking interactive targets.
- **attendance-sessions-workflow-separation**: This decision supersedes the earlier coach-training-operations, coach-attendance, coach-dashboard-attendance-entry and mobile-calendar-attendance-freeze workflow contracts where they conflict. Treat Player Attendance and Staff Attendance as independent domains: their annual colour-coded registers are read-only current-truth views, ordinary player attendance is recorded only against an explicitly selected immutable occurrence, Staff Roll Call records one daily fact per currently supported junior coach, and player rescheduling remains the exceptional adjustment workflow. The Coach Dashboard Attendance card groups Player links for Register, Record and Reschedule separately from Staff links for Register and Roll Call. Calendar owns month/day visibility, static rosters and dated cancellation/replacement; it never edits attendance, though a started scheduled occurrence may open the focused player recorder through a fixed deep link. Sessions exposes Calendar, Create Schedule and Schedules & Rosters as three focused destinations. Preserve existing attendance and scheduling domain rules, SMBA typography, palette, bordered cards, mobile rhythm and personal player/junior-coach registers.
- **junior-coach-dashboard**: Pair the junior-coach workspace with the approved head-coach hero system without its operational briefing ribbon: reuse the same oversized inward-aligned greeting, orthographic badminton-court geometry, quiet line opacity and attendance scroll cue, while retaining the personal attendance message. Present the junior coach's monthly summary as the selected Roll-Call Ledger ticket with a restrained month stamp, editorial attendance percentage, aligned Recorded days, Present and Absent rows, diameter-line-free side notches and one boxed Open attendance record disclosure. Preserve the summary ticket and all self-scoped read-only data rules, but present the expanded record with the same focused-month calendar grammar, direct year navigation and Jump to today behavior as the Player Journal.
- **junior-coach-personal-attendance-calendar**: Replace the junior coach's year-wide horizontal register with the shared focused-month presentation inside the existing Roll-Call Ledger disclosure. Keep Your record and Annual attendance, direct year buttons, Jump to today, URL-backed open/month/year state, previous and next month controls, a centered non-interactive month label, a Monday-first six-week grid and no horizontal scrolling at supported widths. Staff attendance is one self-scoped daily fact: use solid green Present, solid red Absent, a muted Not recorded dash and quiet striped Not available dates before joining or after the India-local reference date; cleared facts read as Not recorded. Keep the adjacent text legend and complete accessible date labels. Do not add player-only training groups, sessions, rescheduling or completion marks, and do not change the monthly summary card, attendance service, write permissions or junior-coach self-read boundary.
- **player-fee-record-annual-ledger**: Use the selected warm-ivory annual fee ledger for the Player Journal's read-only Fee Record. Keep one Your fee record heading, a compact URL-backed year selector, current balance and overall status, then one compact horizontal registration truth band: show Registration fee with its charged amount and Paid when settled, or only the outstanding amount and Due when money remains; omit payment date, fee reference, received and due-date facts from this band. A concession-covered registration may state Covered by concession and never invents a receipt. Present January through December as four columns on desktop and tablet and two on mobile; paid months use pale green, due or partial months use pale red, and quiet months state Before plan, Not issued or Plan ended only when the public record can prove that state. A month is selectable when it has an issued monthly charge or receipt activity, and clicking the open month again collapses it through URL-backed year-only state so Back and Forward restore both open and closed views. Month cells use no red or green status boundaries: retain pale status fills and text, identify selection with an underlined month label plus semantic expanded state, restore the small kink connector between the selected month and its ledger using only the neutral line token, and use a navy keyboard-focus outline. Expanded monthly-fee facts stay charge-scoped and label their total Monthly fee received, while one chronological receipt ledger groups every immutable receipt by the month it was actually received. Registration, monthly and combined receipts use the same full-width vertical rows; each receipt appears once at its full total with its complete public allocation breakdown, and multiple receipts stack newest-first. Receipt-only months and years remain navigable. Keep the expansion compact on desktop and tablet through a narrow month identity and one aligned facts strip, with a roomier mobile reading rhythm and no horizontal scrolling. 
- **player-fee-record-annual-ledger-2**: Preserve browser history with scroll-free links. A partial payment never invents a refund; a true fully paid mid-term withdrawal overrides the numerical Paid status with Closed after withdrawal and shows the withdrawal date, unused-training credit and recorded refund. Registration fees are never presented as refundable.
- **announcements-notice-board**: Treat Announcements as a simple head-coach notice board: write locally, review only the message and its destinations, then publish once. Do not create saved drafts, queues or scheduling. Published content and destinations remain immutable; pinning is mutable display priority and withdrawal is a one-way audited action with a private required reason. Homepage delivery stays failure-isolated from the static marketing shell, while Player Dashboard notices remain authenticated. Preserve SMBA's existing bordered cards, typography and operational-versus-history dashboard pattern.
- **coach-announcement-composer-notice-slip**: Use the selected Concept 01 Notice Slip for /coach/announcements/new. Keep the compact Back to announcements route action, one New announcement heading and one centered fine-bordered slip with a restrained red folded corner and Notice 01 folio. Title and editorial message occupy the body; Homepage and Player Dashboard destinations, pinning, optional expiry and the single Review announcement action form a responsive footer docket. Keep the same four visual bands at every supported width: a full-width Send to label, Homepage and Player Dashboard paired on one row, Pin announcement and Expiry date paired on the next, and one full-width Review announcement action. Mobile tightens the cells without changing that order. Remove redundant page introductions, visually hide neutral helper copy, and do not add drafts, scheduling, an audience picker, attachments or other composer tools. Preserve persistent labels, visible counters, true checkbox semantics, first-invalid focus, the discard warning, the review dialog and idempotent publication navigation.
- **coach-player-attendance-recorder-ledger**: Use the selected Ruled Attendance Ledger for ordinary player attendance marking. Keep the web session register and light beige-white roster in a neutral split view; on tablet and mobile attach the roster directly below the selected navy session before later sessions continue. Remove circular player initials and decorative vertical red keylines. Use meaningful two-digit roster folios, full player names and one joined Present and Absent pressed-state control inside a shared neutral outline; selecting the active choice returns it to Not marked. Selected states use pale fills and corresponding text without green or red lower accent rules. Tablet uses two roster columns, mobile one, while a full-width navy Save attendance action closes the ledger. Preserve eligibility, immutable occurrence identity, rescheduling links, URL state and unsaved-work protection.
- **coach-staff-roll-call-daily-ledger**: Use the selected Daily Staff Ledger for head-coach staff roll call. Flow directly from the compact date docket into one light beige-white ruled register with display-only two-digit folios and full junior-coach names; remove circular initials. Match the player attendance recorder with one joined Present and Absent pressed-state control inside a shared neutral outline and a single neutral divider, using the same 9px desktop/tablet and 8px mobile uppercase typography. Not recorded remains the resting persisted state rather than a third visible action: selecting the active Present or Absent side again clears the mark. Selected states use only restrained pale green or pale red fills and corresponding text—never a coloured lower accent rule. Desktop and tablet keep identity and the joined control aligned on one compact row; mobile places the two equal sides in a second band below identity. Preserve future and pre-joining restrictions, URL-backed date changes, unsaved-work guard, atomic save, feedback and empty-staff state.
